_about: ONE rule, two implementations: the title in use for a held exhibit (Sam, in session, 2026-11-12: "being able to suggest the best canonical title based on what's in use"). kb/title_in_use.py (the Review proposal, kb/_build_exhibits_review.py) and exhibits.js relatedFor + relAligned (the Review card's line, #3160) must give every case below the same answer and hold the same constants. tests/title_in_use_test.py runs the Python side, tests/title_in_use_parity.test.js the JS side. Change the rule in both files and here, or a test fails. `related` is a kb/exhibits_related.json-shaped object: titles [title, issuer index, local titles, colleges, 0 in the reference or 1 proposed, earlier titles]. `expect` is null (nothing named) or {kind, title}; kind is self, in_use_statewide or in_use_most_used. A case may carry own_issuer: true (a credit-by-exam card keeps its own issuer; issuer_for is not applied). A case may carry expect_order: the first titles of relatedFor's rows, in order, which pins the one tie-break: local titles descending, then the lowercased title by code point.
